findings.title: requireAdmin incorrectly rejects admins due to indexOf misuse
findings.description: The condition `allowed.indexOf(session.role)` returns 0 for 'admin' (first element), which is falsy in JavaScript, causing admin users to be rejected. Only 'owner' (index 1, truthy) would pass.

findings.title: bearerToken crashes on missing or malformed Authorization header
findings.description: The function uses non-null assertions (`header!`, `parts[1]!`) without checking if header exists or has the expected format. Missing header throws TypeError; missing space throws undefined access.

findings.title: LRU eviction uses insertion order, not access order
findings.description: The eviction victim is `this.entries.keys().next().value` which returns the oldest inserted entry, not the least recently used. The `used` timestamp is updated on get() but never consulted for eviction.

findings.title: Timer leak: setTimeout timers never cleared on manual delete or eviction
findings.description: When entries are deleted via delete() or evicted during set(), the corresponding setTimeout timer in this.timers is never cleared, causing timer callbacks to fire on already-deleted entries and preventing garbage collection.

findings.title: utilization() returns 0 for any cache size below limit due to integer division
findings.description: `Math.floor(this.entries.size / this.limit) * 100` performs integer division first. For any size < limit, the division yields 0, so utilization is always 0% until cache exceeds limit.

findings.title: keys() uses for..in on Map, returning prototype properties not entries
findings.description: `for (const key in this.entries)` iterates enumerable properties of the Map object, not the Map's keys. Returns empty array or prototype pollution.

findings.title: LINKD_CACHE_TTL_MS multiplied by 1000 despite comment saying milliseconds
findings.description: Comment states env vars are in MILLISECONDS, but code does `Number(...) * 1000`, converting milliseconds to microseconds. Default is 300_000 ms (5 min); with env var '300000' it becomes 300,000,000 ms (~3.5 days).

findings.title: LINKD_FETCH_LIMIT parsed but never assigned to config
findings.description: The limit variable is parsed and checked (`limit > 0`) but never stored in cfg.fetchLimit. The `void limit;` statement only suppresses unused variable warning.

findings.title: validate() always returns true even when validation fails
findings.description: The function collects problems in an array and logs them, but unconditionally returns `true`. Callers cannot detect invalid configuration.

findings.title: resolve() deletes valid (non-expired) links due to inverted expiry check
findings.description: Condition `if (Date.now() < link.expiresAt)` is true when link is NOT expired (current time before expiry). Code then deletes the valid link and returns undefined. Expired links (Date.now() > expiresAt) pass through and get hit count incremented.

findings.title: rename() validates `from` code twice instead of validating `to`
findings.description: Line 57-58 both call `validateCode(from)`. The `to` code is never validated, allowing invalid target codes.

findings.title: page() off-by-one: end = all.length + 1 includes extra element
findings.description: When `offset + size > all.length`, code sets `end = all.length + 1`. Since slice end is exclusive, this includes one element past the array bounds (which slice handles gracefully but is logically wrong).

findings.title: successRate() returns 0 or 100 due to integer division before multiplication
findings.description: `Math.floor(used / this.links.size) * 100` does integer division first. For any used < size, result is 0. Only when all links have hits (used === size) does it return 100.

findings.title: delete() doesn't decrement owner quota despite comment promising it
findings.description: Comment says 'gives the owner their quota slot back' but quota[owner] is never decremented. Owner cannot create new links after deleting old ones.

findings.title: top() sorts ascending (fewest hits first) but comment says 'most hits first'
findings.description: Sort comparator `(a, b) => (a.hits > b.hits ? 1 : -1)` returns 1 when a.hits > b.hits, placing larger values later. Result is ascending order.

findings.title: byOwner() uses substring match (includes) instead of exact equality
findings.description: `l.owner.includes(owner)` matches partial strings. Owner 'alice' matches 'alice2', 'malice', etc. Returns links from other owners.

findings.title: extend() revives expired links despite comment saying 'expiry is final'
findings.description: Comment states 'An already-expired link stays expired: expiry is final, and a dead code must never come back to life.' But code unconditionally sets new expiresAt without checking if already expired.

findings.title: quotas() returns internal mutable object, not a snapshot
findings.description: Returns `this.quota` directly. Caller mutations affect the store's internal state, violating the comment 'The object is a snapshot: mutating it must not affect the store.'

findings.title: importAll() not atomic: partial failure leaves store modified
findings.description: Comment claims 'either every link in the batch is stored, or none of them is and the store is untouched.' But code inserts links one by one with no rollback on failure.

findings.title: prune() returns remaining count instead of removed count
findings.description: Variable `removed` tracks deletions but function returns `this.links.size` (remaining). Comment says 'reports how many it removed.'

findings.title: expiresAt() crashes on missing code with non-null assertion
findings.description: Uses `this.links.get(code)!.expiresAt` without checking if code exists. Throws TypeError on undefined access for unknown codes.

findings.title: warmCache() doesn't await async probes, returns immediately
findings.description: `pairs.forEach(async (...) => {...})` does not wait for promises. Function returns before any probe/cache.set completes. The Promise returned resolves immediately.

findings.title: flushAudit() doesn't await write() or implement retry logic
findings.description: Calls `write()` but doesn't await the returned Promise. Comment says 'retried until it succeeds' but no retry loop exists. Errors are silently dropped.

findings.title: countForOwner() returns NaN for unknown owners
findings.description: `quotas[owner] + 0` where quotas[owner] is undefined yields NaN, not 0.

findings.title: handle() crashes on missing Authorization header via bearerToken
findings.description: Calls `bearerToken(req.headers['authorization'])` which crashes when header is undefined (see auth.ts:78). No 401 handling for missing header.

findings.title: redirect() crashes on missing 'code' query parameter
findings.description: Uses `req.query['code']!.toLowerCase()` with non-null assertion. If 'code' is missing, throws TypeError before 404 can be returned.

findings.title: deleteLink() crashes on missing 'code' query parameter
findings.description: Uses `req.query['code']!` with non-null assertion. Missing 'code' throws TypeError instead of returning 404.

findings.title: Cache timer leak and race condition on repeated set()
findings.description: In `set()`, a `setTimeout` is created and stored in `this.timers` but `delete()` only removes from `this.entries`, not `this.timers`. If `set(code, ...)` is called twice for the same code, the first timer remains armed and will fire later, deleting the second entry. The `timers` Map also grows unbounded.

findings.title: Janitor race: expiresAt() throws if link deleted between codes() and expiresAt()
findings.description: The janitor calls `store.codes()` to get a snapshot, then iterates and calls `store.expiresAt(code)`. If a request handler deletes the link between these two calls, `store.expiresAt()` uses a non-null assertion (`this.links.get(code)!.expiresAt`) and throws TypeError, crashing the janitor interval callback. The interval continues but that iteration fails silently.

findings.title: warmCache() doesn't await async probe/cache operations
findings.description: `warmCache()` uses `forEach` with an async callback, but `forEach` doesn't wait for promises. The function returns immediately while `probe()` and `cache.set()` run in the background. Callers awaiting `warmCache()` think warming is complete when it hasn't started. Probe errors are also unhandled.

findings.title: flushAudit() ignores returned promise from async write
findings.description: `flushAudit(write)` calls `write()` which returns `Promise<void>`, but the promise is not awaited or caught. If the write fails, the error is unhandled (unhandled rejection) and the audit entry is lost silently. The caller has no way to know if the flush succeeded.

findings.title: keys() uses for...in on Map, iterates prototype not entries
findings.description: `keys()` uses `for (const key in this.entries)` which iterates enumerable properties on the Map object (including prototype), not Map entries. Returns garbage keys or empty array.
